2027-04-12.title: Monday after the Second Sunday after Qyomtho · St Julius, Pope
readings: Peace with God; suffering produces endurance, character and hope
Whoever welcomes you welcomes me; a cup of cold water
2027-04-12.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Second Sunday after Qyomtho. Commemoration of St Julius, Pope (Julius I, Bishop of Rome 337–352).
2027-04-12.verse: Therefore, since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
theo: Christ is risen! The first gift of the risen Lord to his frightened disciples was peace: “Peace be with you” (John 20:19). Today St Paul explains what that peace is. “Therefore, since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have obtained access to this grace in which we stand; and we boast in our hope of sharing the glory of God.” Peace with God is not first a calm feeling. It is a new relationship: the enmity of sin is ended, the door is open, and we stand in grace. Christ “was handed over to death for our trespasses and was raised for our justification,” Paul has just written (Romans 4:25). Easter is the reason we can stand before God unafraid. Then Paul says something surprising: “And not only that, but we also boast in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us.” Suffering does not cancel the peace of Easter; in Christ it becomes a road to hope.

Today the Panchangam commemorates St Julius, Bishop of Rome from 337 to 352. His years fell in the storm that followed the Council of Nicaea, when many powerful men sought to soften the faith that the Son is truly God, of one being with the Father. St Athanasius, the bishop of Alexandria who defended that faith, was driven from his see, and he came to Rome. Julius received him, examined his case with a synod in Rome, declared him innocent, and wrote a firm letter to the Eastern bishops who had condemned him, asking why the matter had not been referred to Rome as custom required. Julius did not fear the anger of emperors or bishops; he welcomed the persecuted shepherd. The Gospel of the day reads like a portrait of him: “Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.” In welcoming Athanasius, Julius welcomed Christ, and helped to keep the faith of Nicaea, which we still confess in the Creed at every Holy Qurbono.

Jesus ends with the smallest gift: “and whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones in the name of a disciple, truly I tell you, none of these will lose their reward.” The Fathers loved this verse. St John Chrysostom pointed out that the Lord said “cold” water, so that no one could say he was too poor even to light a fire (in substance). Welcome is within everyone's reach. It may be a refugee family in the next street, a migrant worker from the north at your bus stop, a priest newly transferred to your parish, a student far from home. To welcome them in Christ's name is to welcome Christ, and the Father who sent him. Pray today for the Pope and for all who suffer for the true faith. Then give one cup of cold water: a meal, a phone call, a seat, a word of welcome to someone who needs it. That is the peace of Easter going out from your heart.
outline: Ask: whom have I welcomed this Easter, and whom have I kept outside?
Justified by faith, we stand in grace.
Endurance, character, and a hope that does not disappoint.
Point 3 · Whoever welcomes you welcomes me
St Julius welcomed Athanasius; a cup of cold water.
live: Make one stranger or newcomer feel at home this week: a visit, a meal or a phone call.
Offer one difficulty of this week to God, asking for endurance and hope.
2027-04-12.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you have given us peace with the Father and poured God's love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit. By the prayers of St Julius, who welcomed your persecuted servant Athanasius and guarded the faith of Nicaea, keep our Pope and our bishops firm in the truth. Turn our sufferings into endurance and hope, and make us quick to welcome the least of your brothers and sisters, even with a cup of cold water. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: Through Christ we have access to the grace in which we stand; at the Holy Qurbono he welcomes us to his table, and sends us to welcome others in his name.

quick: Justified by faith, we have peace with God through Jesus Christ and stand in grace.
Suffering produces endurance, character and hope, because God's love is poured into our hearts.
St Julius welcomed St Athanasius; whoever welcomes Christ's messengers, even with a cup of cold water, welcomes Christ.
2027-04-12.action: Welcome one newcomer or stranger this week.
2027-04-12.question: Whom does the Lord want me to welcome in his name?
kidsaint: Julius was the Pope, the bishop of Rome, long ago. A brave bishop named Athanasius was chased out of his city for teaching that Jesus is truly God. Julius welcomed him to Rome, listened to him and stood up for him, even though powerful people were angry. Lesson: stand up for the truth, and be kind to someone others are treating badly.

family.explain: Jesus said that when we welcome his friends, we are welcoming him. Even giving a glass of cold water to someone in his name is something God never forgets. Long ago Pope Julius welcomed a bishop named Athanasius who had nowhere to go. We can welcome people too: a new child in class, a visitor at home, a lonely neighbour.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and for families who have had to leave their homes.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is new or lonely around us, and how can we welcome them?”

illus: A family in Thodupuzha noticed that the young men from Odisha who worked at the construction site near their house ate their lunch sitting on the road. One Sunday after the Holy Qurbono the mother sent her son out with a jug of cold water and a plate of banana fritters. The men were shy at first. Over the next months the family learned their names, and the youngest of them, far from his own mother, began to call her Amma. When the building was finished and the workers left, he came to the gate to say goodbye and could hardly speak. The son said later, “It started with a jug of water.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you give us your peace. Welcome us into your presence now, and teach us to welcome others. Amen.
share: We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). Where do I still live as if God were against me?
Suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope (Romans 5:3–4). What has suffering produced in me?
Whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones (Matthew 10:42). What small welcome can I give this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us people of welcome.
interc: For Pope N. and all the bishops, that like St Julius they may guard the faith with courage.
For those who suffer for the truth of the faith.
For refugees, migrant workers and all who are far from home.
For the sick, that suffering may become hope for them.
For our parish, that every newcomer may find a home among us.
pm.close: Father, through your risen Son you have given us peace and poured your love into our hearts. By the prayers of St Julius, make us strong in the faith and generous in welcome, that in receiving the least we may receive Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The first word of the risen Lord to his disciples was peace. St Paul tells us what it means: since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). We stand in grace, unafraid.

Even suffering is changed. Suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit (Romans 5:3–5).

Today we remember St Julius, Pope. When St Athanasius was driven out of Alexandria for defending the faith that the Son is truly God, Julius welcomed him in Rome and stood up for him. Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, says Jesus (Matthew 10:40).
Welcome is within everyone's reach: even a cup of cold water given in his name will not lose its reward. Let us give someone that cup this week: a meal, a visit, a word of welcome. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus said that if we give even a glass of cold water to someone in his name, God will never forget it. Long ago Pope Julius welcomed a bishop who had been chased away. Can you welcome someone this week, maybe a new child in your class? When you welcome them, you are welcoming Jesus!

intro: Theme: “Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.”
On the commemoration of St Julius, Pope: the peace of Easter, the hope that suffering produces, and the welcome that receives Christ.

sub: Access to the grace in which we stand.
q: the Lord lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
points.apply: Make your peace with God this Easter season in the sacrament of Reconciliation, and with one person you have hurt.

sub: A hope that does not disappoint.
q: But he knows the way that I take; when he has tested me, I shall come out like gold.
My brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of any kind, consider it nothing but joy, because you know that the testing of your faith produces endurance;
points.apply: Offer one difficulty this week to the risen Lord, and ask him for endurance and hope.

sub: He guarded the faith of Nicaea.
q: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Give one cup of cold water this week: a meal, a visit or a word of welcome to someone far from home.

concl: The risen Lord has given us peace with God, and in him even suffering becomes hope.
St Julius welcomed the persecuted shepherd and so welcomed Christ.
2027-04-12.resolve: Stand firm in the faith we confess in the Creed, and welcome the least in the name of Jesus.
